author: West Central Reporter
title: Western Illinois football recognized with multiple Phil Steele postseason honors
text:
Western Illinois University Leathernecks Men's Football | Western Illinois University Leathernecks
Western Illinois University Leathernecks Men's Football | Western Illinois University Leathernecks
Western Illinois University's football team has received several postseason honors as part of the 2025 Phil Steele FCS awards. Ten Leatherneck players were named to the Phil Steele OVC-Big South All-Conference teams, which recognize athletes from all areas of play.
Markell Holman, Jr., running back, and Christian Pierce, Sr., linebacker, earned First Team All-OVC-Big South honors. Demari Davis, Sr., wide receiver, was named to the Second Team. The Third Team included Alex Williams, Sr., tight end; Justin Richardson, Sr., defensive back; and Malini Ti'a, Sr., defensive back. Fourth Team selections were Christian Anaya, Jr., wide receiver; Dagen Miller, Sr., offensive lineman; James Durand, sophomore offensive lineman; and Kevin Washington, Sr., linebacker.
In addition to conference recognition, Payne Miller was selected as a Third Team Phil Steele FCS Freshman All-American for his performance on the defensive line.
According to Western Illinois University’s official website https://goleathernecks.com/sports/football, the Leathernecks compete in the Ohio Valley Conference-Big South Football Association and have a history that includes conference titles in 1997 and 1998 along with playoff appearances. The program is led by head coach Joe Davis and plays its home games at Hanson Field on campus. The team is known for its military-inspired toughness and tradition since adopting the "Fighting Leathernecks" nickname with U.S. Navy permission in 1927.
The university highlights its commitment to player development and competitive seasons through its football program https://goleathernecks.com/sports/football.
"The postseason honors reflect the continued development and competitiveness of the Leathernecks within the OVC-Big South Conference and on the national FCS stage."
Western Illinois aims to build on this momentum as it prepares for the 2026 season.
For more information about Leatherneck Football or updates on their activities, visit GoLeathernecks.com or follow their social media channels.
